title: Derived scalar conjugate and group-restriction interchange
statement:
Fix the small coherent profinite site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, morphisms and all section sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $J,H$ be topological groups. Write $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ for internal $R$-modules with a natural $\underline J$-action by linear automorphisms [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the normalized functors of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]: $T_J$ is trivial inflation, $\Gamma_{R,J}$ is the invariant subsheaf with its specified inclusion, $L_J=D(T_J)$, $F_J=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ with its canonical computation unit $\alpha_J$, and $L_J\dashv F_J$ is the canonical derived adjunction, with unit $\eta_J$ and counit $\varepsilon_J$. For a continuous homomorphism $u:H\to J$ put $U=D(u^*)$.

Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be any condensed ring map. Let $s_0,s_J,s_H$ be scalar restrictions on the base and action modules and on their derived categories, $E_0,E_J,E_H$ their derived scalar-extension left adjoints [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], and $U'=D(u^*)$ for $R'$-actions. Use the normalized scalar comparisons of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]. Regard $L_J^R,L_J^{R'}$ and $E_0,E_J$ as the derived module pullbacks along the ringed-topos morphisms $p_J$ and the coefficient morphisms induced by $\varphi$ of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], whose square commutes with identity comparison on underlying sheaves. The conjugate of the derived pullback comparison
$$E_JL_J^R\xrightarrow{\sim}L_J^{R'}E_0,$$
obtained from that commuting square by the canonical composition comparisons $c_{f,g}$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], is a natural isomorphism
$$d_J:F_J^Rs_J\xrightarrow{\sim}s_0F_J^{R'}.$$
It is normalized by the computation units and the equality of fixed-section submodules $\Gamma_{R,J}s_J=s_0\Gamma_{R',J}$. Explicitly on every complex $P'$,
$$d_{J,QP'}\circ\alpha^R_{J,C(s_J)P'}=s_0(\alpha^{R'}_{J,P'})$$
under the termwise scalar identifications. It commutes with canonical shifts and hence with image-triangle connecting arrows. No flatness of $\varphi$ and no preservation of injectives by scalar restriction are assumed.

Write $b^A_u:F^A_J\to F^A_HD(u^*)$, for $A=R,R\prime$, for the derived invariant-inclusion transformation normalized as in [lem-sfb-condensed-restriction-mate-normalization]. For all $N\in D(\mathcal A_R(J))$, $N'\in D(\mathcal A_{R'}(J))$ and $f:N\to s_JN'$, put $c_J(f)=d_{J,N'}\circ F_J^R(f)$. Then in $D(\mathcal M_R)$,
$$c_H(Uf)\circ b^R_{u,N}=s_0(b^{R'}_{u,N'})\circ c_J(f),$$
using the localized underlying identity $Us_J=s_HU'$. Under the composite adjunction bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(X,s_0F_H^{R'}U'N')\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_H^RX,s_HU'N'),$$
both displayed composites, for $X=F_J^RN$, have transpose $U(f)\circ U(\varepsilon^R_{J,N})$. All equalities hold as derived arrows before applying homology.

proof.text: Use the action-site realization for the sheaves of groups $\underline J,\underline H$. The infrastructure lemma supplies that these are sheaves, that the internal module and action categories are Grothendieck abelian, and that trivial inflation, group restriction along a continuous group homomorphism, and scalar restriction are additive and exact. The present $u:H\to J$ is such a homomorphism: its continuity gives the sectionwise map $C(S,H)\to C(S,J)$, and its group laws make this a morphism of group sheaves, so the current infrastructure hypothesis applies. The action-topos lemma identifies trivial inflation with module pullback along $p_J$, and identifies all coefficient squares as ringed-topos squares with identity underlying-sheaf comparison. In particular the two scalar/inflation composites have the same ordinary right adjoint: on a test object both select precisely those sections of the same underlying module fixed after every base change. The scalar action on this submodule is the restricted $R$-action. The invariant inclusions and both ordinary Hom transposes therefore agree, not just the underlying invariant objects. Exact functors descend termwise with the indicated signed shifts.

proof.text: Apply the ringed derived composition and geometric-isomorphism comparisons to the two paths from $(\mathscr E^J,R'_J)$ to $(\mathscr E,R)$. Their left adjoints are $E_JL_J^R$ and $L_J^{R'}E_0$. This gives the specified isomorphism $\theta_J:E_JL_J^R\simeq L_J^{R'}E_0$. The scalar balancing lemma, applied to $p_J$ and $R\to R'$, identifies it with the scalar-adjunction mate of the exact identity $\chi_J:L_J^Rs_0\simeq s_JL_J^{R'}$: on flat-term K-flat representatives both are the balancing map preserving insertion $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Every complex has a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], so by naturality the two isomorphisms agree on the whole derived category. For the two composite adjunctions their right adjoints are $F_J^Rs_J$ and $s_0F_J^{R'}$. Conjugation of $\theta_J$ gives the isomorphism $d_J$ in the stated direction. Conjugation of its inverse is its inverse. This uses neither flatness of the coefficient map nor injective preservation by scalar restriction.

proof.text:
Here is the computation-unit normalization. Choose normalized lifts of the common composite $k:(\mathscr E^J,R'_J)\to(\mathscr E,R)$ and of the two paths, using the adjoint-lift lemma. Let $a:Rk_*\simeq F_J^Rs_J$ and $a':Rk_*\simeq s_0F_J^{R'}$ be their right comparison isomorphisms, including the specified identity geometric comparison. By the composition-comparison lemma these are the conjugates of the pullback comparisons and obey the right-derived-unit composition formula on every complex. The two-isomorphism comparison obeys the same unit normalization, so the specified identity geometric comparison introduces no extra automorphism. Since scalar restriction is exact, its derived computation unit is the exact-localization identification. Thus, writing $\alpha_k$ for the computation unit of $Rk_*$, these formulas are
$$a_{QP'}\alpha_{k,P'}=\alpha^R_{J,C(s_J)P'},\qquad a'_{QP'}\alpha_{k,P'}=s_0(\alpha^{R'}_{J,P'}).$$
Conjugation respects composition, hence $d_J=a'a^{-1}$. Substitution proves the requested equation for every $P'$, without claiming that $C(s_J)P'$ is K-injective. The ordinary right comparison here is the fixed-section identity of step 1.

proof.text:
Record the Hom normalization needed for the interchange. Put $\tau_{J,Y}=s_J(\varepsilon^{R'}_{J,Y})\circ\chi_{J,F_J^{R'}Y}$. The composite Hom bijection of the statement takes $a:X\to s_0F_J^{R'}Y$ to $\tau_{J,Y}\circ L_J^R(a)$. Indeed, first transpose across $E_0\dashv s_0$, then across $L_J^{R'}\dashv F_J^{R'}$, precompose with $\theta_{J,X}$, and transpose back across $E_J\dashv s_J$. The assertion that $\theta_J$ is the scalar mate of $\chi_J$ says exactly that this composite is the displayed formula. Conjugation says equivalently that it takes $d_{J,Y}\circ z$ to the ordinary $L_J^R\dashv F_J^R$ transpose of $z:X\to F_J^Rs_JY$. Taking $z=1$ gives
$$\tau_{J,Y}\circ L_J^R(d_{J,Y})=\varepsilon^R_{J,s_JY}. \tag{*}$$
Taking the transpose of $\tau_{J,Y}$ also gives the explicit inverse formula
$$d_{J,Y}^{-1}=F_J^R(s_J\varepsilon^{R'}_{J,Y})\circ F_J^R(\chi_{J,F_J^{R'}Y})\circ\eta^R_{J,s_0F_J^{R'}Y}.$$
These are consequences of the specified mate and conjugate formulas and composite Hom bijections, not an additional base-change theorem. The same formulas hold with $H$ in place of $J$.

proof.text:
The last formula expresses $d_J^{-1}$ using only $\chi_J$, the derived inflation/invariant adjunction unit and counit, and whiskering/composition with exact scalar restriction. The infrastructure lemma supplies shift compatibility of those units and counits and the canonical termwise shifts of the exact functors. The components of $\chi_J$ are identity maps on shifted underlying complexes, hence commute with these shifts. The composition-and-whiskering lemma therefore shows that $d_J^{-1}$ commutes with every canonical shift, and inversion of that square proves the same for $d_J$. For a triangle $A'\to B'\to C'\xrightarrow{\delta'}A'[1]$, naturality gives
$$d_{J,A'[1]}\,F_J^Rs_J(\delta')=s_0F_J^{R'}(\delta')\,d_{J,C'}.$$
Replace $d_{J,A'[1]}$ by its shifted component using the preceding square. This is precisely the square of the image-triangle connecting arrows, with the canonical signed shift comparisons. Both image rows are distinguished because invariants and exact scalar restriction are triangulated by the cited infrastructure and exact-factorization lemmas.

proof.text:
Write $X=F_J^RN$ and $Y=U'N'$, so $s_HY=Us_JN'$. The group-restriction normalization lemma gives
$$\varepsilon^R_{H,UN}\circ L_H^R(b^R_{u,N})=U(\varepsilon^R_{J,N})$$
under $L_H^R=UL_J^R$, and its primed version gives the corresponding identity over $R'$. By (*) for $H$, the transpose of the left displayed composite is
$$\begin{aligned}
&\tau_{H,Y}L_H^R(d_{H,Y}F_H^R(Uf)b^R_{u,N})\\
&=\varepsilon^R_{H,s_HY}L_H^RF_H^R(Uf)L_H^R(b^R_{u,N})\\
&=U(f)\varepsilon^R_{H,UN}L_H^R(b^R_{u,N})\\
&=U(f)U(\varepsilon^R_{J,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is counit naturality. This is a computation in the ordinary derived category, not an equality after homology.

proof.text:
Put $a=d_{J,N'}F_J^R(f):X\to s_0F_J^{R'}N'$. Naturality of $\chi_H$ and the primed group-restriction counit formula give the transpose of the other composite as
$$\begin{aligned}
&\tau_{H,Y}L_H^R(s_0(b^{R'}_{u,N'})a)\\
&=s_H(\varepsilon^{R'}_{H,Y}L_H^{R'}(b^{R'}_{u,N'}))\,\chi_{H,F_J^{R'}N'}L_H^R(a)\\
&=s_H(U'\varepsilon^{R'}_{J,N'})\,\chi_{H,F_J^{R'}N'}L_H^R(a)\\
&=U\bigl(\tau_{J,N'}L_J^R(a)\bigr)\\
&=U\bigl(\varepsilon^R_{J,s_JN'}L_J^RF_J^R(f)\bigr)\\
&=U(f)U(\varepsilon^R_{J,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
For the third equality, $s_HU'=Us_J$, $L_H^R=UL_J^R$ and $L_H^{R'}=U'L_J^{R'}$ are the localized underlying identities; the identity components defining $\chi$ give $\chi_H=U\chi_J$ under them. The fourth equality uses (*), and the last is counit naturality. The composite adjunction bijection is injective, so the two derived arrows agree, with exactly the stated common transpose.
